title: PRD: Incident-derived detection & mitigation for silent inference regressions
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: A recent production regression that increased hallucination rate by ~3.5% after a kernel mapping change went undetected because standard latency/error SLOs remained healthy. Postmortem recommended adding product-level requirements to detect and halt silent quality regressions (accuracy/hallucination/semantic-rank shifts) before wide rollout. This ticket captures PRD updates and acceptance criteria to convert those postmortem action items into verifiable shipping requirements for model/runtime releases.
background: Incident snapshot: a kernel-optimizer rollout altered numerical precision on a subset of transformer kernels. Token latency and error rates were unchanged; however automated reranking and downstream QA flagged user complaints two days later. Root cause analysis determined the change caused subtle logits shifts, amplifying low-confidence hallucinations in edge prompts. Existing traffic-based A/B checks didn't surface the issue because traffic signals were sparse for the affected prompt cohort.
goals: 1) Define PRD requirements that force objective, reproducible quality checks for every runtime/model release. 2) Add telemetry and gating to catch 'silent' regressions (quality-first signals) before 100% rollout. 3) Specify operational behavior (automated rollback / canary shepherding / alerting) to reduce MTTD/MTTR for quality degradations.
proposed_solution: A layered approach: (a) Quality-first canaries: every release must run a golden-prompt suite (deterministic prompts + expected structured outputs) against representative model variants and kernel configs. (b) Statistical drift detectors: track distributional and metric deltas (logit-shift, perplexity-on-holdout, rerank-AUC) with configurable SRO thresholds. (c) Automatic hold-and-fallback: if quality thresholds fail in canary, the deployment should automatically pin to the previous compatible variant and open an incident. (d) Telemetry enrichment: add prompt cohort tagging, token-level scoring, and a quality-change timeline to the Console. (e) Playback harness: ability to replay sampled failed requests against previous baseline for triage and RCA.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Golden-prompt suite integrated into the release pipeline and runs as a pre-rollout gating job (pass/fail).
2) At least three quality metrics are computed per run (logit-shift magnitude, rerank-AUC delta, holdout-perplexity) and stored in time-series with 90-day retention.
3) Alerting policy created: quality-signal breach triggers P0 incident and marks release "on-hold" automatically in the Console.
4) Rollout automation: failed canary automatically reverts to last-known-good variant within 10 minutes and prevents escalation to 100% traffic.
5) Console UI surfaces cohort-level diffs for the golden prompts with links to the failing request samples and a one-click replay-to-baseline action.
6) Engineering runbook updated with triage steps that leverage the playback harness and defines ownership for rollback decisions.
7) Regression test coverage: CI includes at least 25 golden prompts covering high-risk customer flows (billing summaries, policy classification, search rerank edge cases).
8) Synthetic end-to-end canary runs documented and executed in two recent releases as validation before this ticket is closed.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement golden-prompt CI job and console telemetry hooks; deploy to staging. Phase 2 (3 weeks): implement statistical detectors and automated hold logic in canary controller; pilot on one low-risk model-channel pair with human-in-loop alerts. Phase 3 (2 weeks): expand to top-5 most-used models and enable automated rollback on quality breaches. Post-launch (ongoing): monitor false positive rate, adjust thresholds, and add new prompt cohorts every two sprints.
success_metrics: - Reduction in customer-reported quality incidents from regressions by >= 60% for releases using the gated flow within 90 days. - Mean time to detect quality regression (MTTD-quality) reduced from days to < 30 minutes for gated releases. - False-positive hold rate below 5% after 90 days of tuning.
notes: Design & Eng collaboration required: Console product work to show cohort diffs + playback; Runtime work to surface logit and rerank metrics; CI infra to run golden prompts efficiently. Consider storage/compute cost tradeoffs for long retention of prompt-level telemetry. Add dedicated label for experimental thresholds to avoid noisy production firing during tuning.
